claim: Kiln published its postmortem on 7 October 2025.
The entry point was a compromised GitHub token belonging to a Kiln infrastructure engineer.
locator: Incident description paragraph beginning The investigation has determined
evidence: GitHub access token belonging to a Kiln infrastructure engineer
qualification: Kiln's investigation; origin of token compromise not established.

claim: The actor created and immediately deleted branches to trigger CI/CD workflows and harvested stored secrets and cloud credentials.
locator: Incident description paragraphs beginning The malicious actor and From the triggered
evidence: created and immediately deleted branches; harvested stored secrets and cloud credentials

claim: The actor injected a payload into a running Kubernetes pod serving the Kiln Connect API and changed one endpoint's logic.
locator: Incident description paragraph beginning The threat actor injected
evidence: payload into a running Kubernetes pod; modifying the logic of a Kiln API endpoint

claim: The changed endpoint returned a malicious transaction alongside the expected deactivate-stake transaction.
locator: Incident description paragraph beginning The threat actor injected
evidence: malicious transaction, in addition to the expected deactivate stake transaction
qualification: Kiln's wording; SwissBorg describes extra instructions.

claim: The trigger concerned the existing withdrawal authority of the stake account supplied in the POST having stake balances above 150k SOL.
locator: Incident description paragraph beginning The threat actor injected
evidence: only if the existing withdrawal authority of the stake account provided in the POST call held stake balances above 150k SOL
qualification: This does not say that the individual stake account named in the POST held above 150k SOL.

claim: One Kiln client used Dashboard to unstake a SOL stake account on 31 August 2025; the malicious transaction was forwarded to custody and approved by a quorum.
locator: Incident description paragraph beginning One Kiln client
evidence: August 31st; forwarded from Kiln Dashboard to custody; approved by a quorum of signatories
qualification: Kiln does not name the client in this paragraph; SwissBorg identifies itself as affected.

claim: Kiln said it consistently recommended decoding before signing and linked a tool from its Dashboard and documentation.
locator: Incident description paragraphs beginning To avoid any risk and Kiln provides
evidence: consistently recommended; provides a decoding tool linked from Dashboard

claim: Kiln said it found no evidence of any other malicious transaction or customer loss.
locator: Executive summary paragraph beginning There is no evidence; incident description paragraph beginning At this time
evidence: no evidence of any other malicious transaction or loss of funds from any other Kiln customers
qualification: No-evidence statement, not proof that no other effect occurred.

locator: Publication line and first two body paragraphs
evidence: 8 September 2025; funds improperly removed; paused Solana staking
qualification: Initial joint statement says possible unauthorized wallet access, not a final forensic finding.
